context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a EU-compliant platform designed for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It guarantees strict data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
* **Personas:** Library Patrons, Librarians / Circulation Staff, Library Administrators, Third-Party Vendors / Digital Content Providers.
* **Core System:** Library Management System.
* **External Systems:** EU Payment Gateway, Notification Service.
* **Containers:** Asynchronous Staging Container, Internal Message Broker, Core Search and Circulation microservices.

## Relationships
* **Library Patrons, Librarians, Administrators -> Library Management System:** HTTPS (TLS 1.3), OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authentication.
* **Library Management System -> EU Payment Gateway:** HTTPS/REST protocols.
* **Library Management System -> Notification Service:** HTTPS/SMTP protocols via message broker.
* **Third-Party Vendors -> Library Management System:** SFTP / HTTPS REST webhooks.
* **Internal Containers:** mTLS with SPIFFE/SPIRE workload identities.

## Technology Stack
* **Edge & Routing:** Geo-DNS and Anycast CDN constrained to EU Points of Presence to meet performance SLAs.
* **Message Broker:** EU-hosted Kafka or RabbitMQ for asynchronous notification decoupling.
* **Security & Secrets:** HashiCorp Vault / AWS KMS EU for secrets management; AES-256 and TLS 1.3 for data protection.
* **Observability:** W3C Trace Context for distributed tracing across services.

## Rationale
This architecture enforces strict EU data residency and GDPR compliance while maintaining isolated asynchronous ingestion to meet the sub-800ms search latency requirement. Secure zero-trust controls ensure robust data protection across all internal and external touchpoints.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It adheres strictly to EU-only data residency requirements while ensuring high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons, Librarians/Circulation Staff, Library Administrators, Third-Party Vendors/Digital Content Providers
- Single Page Application (SPA)
- API Gateway
- Core Domain Container
- Search Container
- Integration Container
- Async Event Broker
- EU Payment Gateway, Notification Service
- EU-hosted PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch

## Relationships
- SPA to API Gateway: HTTPS/REST
- API Gateway to Core Domain/Search/Integration: gRPC or REST over TLS within EU-isolated VPC
- Core Domain to EU-hosted PostgreSQL: Database protocol over TLS
- Integration Container to EU Payment Gateway & Notification Service: HTTPS
- Core Domain to Async Event Broker: Domain events publishing (SASL/SCRAM, mTLS)
- Integration Container to Async Event Broker: Asynchronous consumption with DLQs

## Technology Stack
- React/TypeScript: SPA framework for intuitive user experience
- Nginx or Spring Cloud Gateway: API Gateway for request routing
- Java/Spring Boot: Core Domain Container for robust cataloguing and circulation (R-01)
- Elasticsearch: Dedicated Search Container for sub-800ms search performance (R-05)
- Node.js/TypeScript: Integration Container for external APIs and payment handling
- Apache Kafka or RabbitMQ: Async Event Broker for decoupled event-driven notifications
- Kubernetes (EKS/AKS) & ArgoCD: Container orchestration and declarative GitOps deployment
- PostgreSQL: EU-hosted transactional database with encryption-at-rest (CMK)

## Rationale
This architecture isolates user-facing workflows and decouples search and notification processing to consistently achieve the required 99th-percentile search response time under 800ms. Strict containerization, mTLS, and regional hosting enforce EU-only data residency compliance and enterprise security.

Single Page Application (SPA).analysis:
## Overview
• Single Page Application (SPA) providing self-service patron portals and staff circulation workflows for the Library Management System.
• Centralizes user interactions while adhering strictly to EU data residency and WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility mandates.

## Key Elements
• Library Patrons, Librarians/Circulation Staff, Library Administrators
• Single Page Application (SPA) Container
• Routing & Authentication Module
• Catalog & Search Component
• Circulation & Admin Workspace
• API Client Layer (HTTP Interceptor) & State/Cache Manager
• API Gateway

## Relationships
• Library Patrons/Staff/Administrators -> Single Page Application (SPA): Interacts with portal and workspace via `[HTTPS/REST]`
• Single Page Application (SPA) -> API Gateway: Sends user requests and proxies session handling via `[HTTPS/REST/JSON]`
• Nginx Container -> Client Browser: Delivers static assets using `[HTTPS/TLS 1.3]` with EU-only edge pinning

## Technology Stack
• React with TypeScript: Core frontend library for building type-safe, component-driven user interfaces.
• Nginx: High-performance web server for serving static assets and enforcing Content Security Policy (CSP) headers.
• Docker & Global CDN: Immutable containerization and EU-pinned edge nodes for deployment and data residency compliance.

## Rationale
• The decoupled React/TypeScript architecture isolates high-frequency search input to help achieve the sub-800ms performance NFR.
• Centralizing security controls and API interactions ensures robust XSS mitigation, strict token handling, and EU data residency compliance.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for academic and public libraries. The architecture enforces strict EU data residency while maintaining high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
- **Library Patrons & Librarians/Staff**: End users accessing portals via the SPA.
- **Single Page Application (SPA)**: React/TypeScript frontend served via Nginx.
- **API Gateway**: Spring Cloud Gateway handling edge routing, security, and policies.
- **Core Domain Container**: Java/Spring Boot handling circulation and cataloging with PostgreSQL (EU-hosted).
- **Search Container**: Elasticsearch handling catalog queries.
- **Integration Container**: Node.js/TypeScript handling external integrations.
- **Redis Cluster**: In-memory store for rate limiting.

## Relationships
- **SPA -> API Gateway**: Sends user requests over HTTPS/REST.
- **API Gateway -> Core Domain / Search / Integration**: Forwards traffic via gRPC or REST over TLS using mutual TLS (mTLS) within an EU-isolated VPC.
- **API Gateway -> Redis Cluster**: Evaluates traffic quotas and rate limits.

## Technology Stack
- **Spring Cloud Gateway**: Selected for native JVM ecosystem integration, security filters, and circuit breaker support.
- **Redis**: Deployed as an EU-isolated cluster for distributed rate limiting.
- **PostgreSQL & Elasticsearch**: Backend data stores restricted to EU data residency.
- **OpenTelemetry**: Used for distributed tracing and latency tracking to meet SLAs.

## Rationale
The Spring Cloud Gateway architecture centralizes security, rate limiting, and request normalization at the edge. This protects backend services, ensures strict EU compliance, and supports the required <800ms search performance SLA.

Core Domain Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. The Core Domain Container handles cataloguing, circulation logic, and transactional data storage while strictly enforcing EU data residency.

## Key Elements
- Core Domain Container (Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.2, OCI distroless image)
- Cataloguing Component (Spring Data JPA)
- Circulation Component (Domain-Driven Design / Spring Transaction)
- Outbox Pattern Component & Debezium / JDBC Poller
- Audit & Compliance Component (Spring Data Envers / append-only tables)
- Security & Context Propagation Component (Spring Security, OAuth2/OIDC JWT)
- PostgreSQL 16 (EU-hosted, native tablespace encryption)
- Async Event Broker (Apache Kafka)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Core Domain Container: Routes domain and circulation requests [gRPC or REST over TLS within EU-isolated VPC]
- Core Domain Container -> EU-hosted PostgreSQL: Persists transactional and audit data [Database protocol over TLS 1.3 with certificate pinning]
- Core Domain Container -> Async Event Broker: Publishes scrubbed domain events [SASL/SCRAM, mTLS]

## Technology Stack
- Java 21 / Spring Boot 3.2: Modern runtime for robust domain logic and performance.
- Spring Modulith: Enforces strict package boundaries between domain components.
- PostgreSQL 16: Relational storage with row-level security and `pg_partman` for EU data residency compliance.
- Spring Security & OAuth2: Handles JWT validation and fine-grained RBAC.
- OpenTelemetry / Micrometer: Enables comprehensive observability of JVM metrics and outbox lag.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict EU data residency via isolated cloud infrastructure and CMEK encryption while maintaining high performance. The Transactional Outbox pattern guarantees reliable event delivery to meet sub-800ms search requirements without sacrificing data consistency.

Search Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue items and manage circulation. The architecture utilizes a unified Search Service to deliver sub-800ms search performance while enforcing EU data residency.

## Key Elements
- Search Service (Java/Spring Boot)
- Search Index (Elasticsearch 8.x)
- Async Event Broker (Apache Kafka)
- API Gateway (Nginx / Spring Cloud Gateway)
- Core Domain Container (PostgreSQL)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Search Service: `REST/JSON over TLS`
- Search Service -> Search Index: `Elasticsearch Native Bolt/REST with mTLS`
- Search Service -> Async Event Broker: `Kafka Protocol over TLS`

## Technology Stack
- Java / Spring Boot: Unified runtime for search routing, synchronization, and analytics
- Elasticsearch 8.x: Scalable storage with fuzzy matching and faceted search support
- Apache Kafka: Asynchronous event streaming for eventual consistency and telemetry
- Kubernetes: Container orchestration with strict resource limits and persistent volume encryption

## Rationale
Unifying the search runtime into a single Java/Spring Boot service reduces operational complexity while meeting stringent EU data residency and security mandates. Elasticsearch configurations and Resilience4j circuit breakers guarantee the 800ms performance SLA.

Integration Container.analysis:
## Overview
- Solution: Library Management System for public and academic libraries to catalogue items and manage circulation.
- Core Purpose: Manages external APIs, third-party digital content ingestion, and secure payment processing within EU data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
- Integration Container (Node.js/TypeScript)
- Webhook Handler Component (Node.js/Express)
- Vendor Ingestion Service (Node.js/TypeScript with Zod)
- Outbox Dispatcher Component
- Audit Logging Component (Node.js/Winston or Pino)
- Third-Party Vendors / Digital Content Providers
- EU Payment Gateway
- Async Event Broker (Apache Kafka/RabbitMQ)
- Core Domain Container (PostgreSQL, EU-hosted)

## Relationships
- Third-Party Vendors -> Vendor Ingestion Service: Ingests digital content [HTTPS / SFTP with TLS 1.3]
- EU Payment Gateway -> Webhook Handler Component: Sends secure financial webhooks [HTTPS with HMAC verification]
- Outbox Dispatcher -> Async Event Broker: Publishes events reliably [SASL/SCRAM, mTLS]
- Audit Logging Component -> Core Domain Container: Persists immutable audit trails [gRPC/REST over TLS within EU-isolated VPC]
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicies: Enforces egress allowlisting to authorized payment gateways and vendors only

## Technology Stack
- Node.js & TypeScript: Chosen for asynchronous I/O performance in integration workloads
- Zod: Provides strict schema validation for untrusted external payloads
- Kubernetes & HPA: Enables proactive scaling based on event broker queue depth and SFTP payload volume
- OpenTelemetry: Implements end-to-end distributed tracing across components
- Secrets Manager: Injects API keys and SFTP private keys securely without environment variables

## Rationale
- Decomposing the Integration Container into isolated components satisfies the 5-minute digital content ingestion SLA and ensures resilience against transient gateway timeouts.
- Mandatory cryptographic verification, strict network egress rules, and EU-hosted audit logging enforce required data residency and financial security constraints.

Async Event Broker.analysis:
## Overview
[A resilient Library Management System providing cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. Built with strict EU-only data residency guarantees.]

## Key Elements
* Apache Kafka (Async Event Broker container, deployed via Strimzi operator across 3 EU availability zones)
* KRaft Metadata Quorum (Replaces ZooKeeper for broker state management)
* Confluent Schema Registry (Co-located within Strimzi footprint for Avro schema validation)
* Core Domain Container (Java/Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, publishes domain events)
* Integration Container (Node.js/TypeScript, consumes events asynchronously with DLQs)
* HashiCorp Vault / Kubernetes Secrets (Dynamic credential rotation)

## Relationships
* Core Domain Container -> Apache Kafka: Publishes domain events via [mTLS, SASL/SCRAM-512]
* Integration Container -> Apache Kafka: Consumes events and reads DLQs via [mTLS, SASL/SCRAM-512]
* Apache Kafka -> Apache Kafka: Inter-broker communication secured via [Internal mTLS]
* Strimzi Operator -> Apache Kafka: Manages deployment and KRaft consensus

## Technology Stack
* Apache Kafka: Append-only log architecture chosen for event sourcing and partition-level ordering.
* Strimzi Operator: Kubernetes operator for automated multi-AZ broker deployment and lifecycle management.
* KRaft: Eliminates ZooKeeper to reduce operational complexity and failure modes.
* Avro / Confluent Schema Registry: Co-located to enforce contract compatibility without excessive SRE overhead.
* mTLS & SASL/SCRAM-512: Mandated for all client-broker and inter-broker authentication/encryption.
* LUKS: Persistent volume encryption protecting EU data at rest.

## Rationale
[This event-driven architecture decouples heavy third-party integrations and notifications from core cataloging, ensuring high availability and compliance with the 99th-percentile search response SLA (<800 ms). Strict security, encryption, and partitioning enforce EU data residency and GDPR mandates.]
